title: Should libsail replace nail's own parsing and indexing of its inputs?
body:
nail parses and indexes its fasta and p7hmm inputs itself, in `nail/src/io`. The question was whether `libsail` should replace that code. The serial-overhead work under nail-1964b2 waited on the answer, since the target db write, the profile parse and the index passes all sit on that code.

The current code runs a single-threaded index pass in 1 MiB reads, line by line. HMM files get a `strum` string match per line, and the index is an `IndexMap<String, Offset>` keyed by name. nail then reads records back one at a time with a seek and a `read_exact`, and parses each on demand. A parallel index build exists, since `Index::build` is generic over `CHUNKS` and tested up to 32, but `from_path` hard-codes `CHUNKS=1`.
close_reason: The outcome note has the decision. nail keeps `Sequence` and `Profile` and moves its io onto `libsail`'s `Framed` in nail-167dd7. The two serial fixes no longer wait on this.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/2aff5e6c
notes.text:
Outcome. `libsail` was read at 0.4.0 and nail on `dev` at `432ff65`.

## libsail's types do not replace `Sequence` and `Profile`

`FastaRecord` holds a name, a description and residue bytes. `HmmRecord` holds the header and the model as HMMER's negative log probabilities. libnail's `Sequence` holds digital bytes with a sentinel at each end. `Profile` holds tables that `ProfileBuilder::build` derives: log-odds match scores against background, entry transitions from an occupancy recursion, ambiguity scores and a consensus. No parse can produce those, so a conversion step exists either way. Traits in libnail standing in for the two types would abstract over fields the DP code never reads.

## nail uses libsail's framing and indexing and parses records itself

The design under discussion is a struct named `Framed<S: Source>` in `libsail`, holding a byte source and an `Index`. Its `record(n)` returns the raw bytes of record `n`. `IndexedFasta`, `IndexedHmm` and `IndexedStockholm` become wrappers over it, so `sail` keeps its call sites. nail wraps it in its own `Fasta` and `P7Hmm` and parses the bytes into `Sequence` and `Profile`. That work is nail-167dd7.

## Rejected

- `Indexed<P: Parse, D: Delimit, S: Source>`. nail uses no delimiter of its own, so the type parameter buys it nothing. Dropping `Format` from `Index` would also remove the check in `IndexedFasta::with_index` that refuses an index built for another format.
- `Indexed<P: Parse, S: Source>` with type aliases. Jack turned it down as a new abstraction that `Framed` makes unnecessary.

## mmseqs databases are a separate question

An mmseqs database stores null-terminated records and takes its offsets from a `.index` file, so scanning for a delimiter is the wrong way to frame it. `Index::new(format, offsets)` could take offsets loaded from that file, but `Format` has no variant for it. The prefilter database is also split over `pdb.0` to `pdb.3`, which one `Source` does not cover. Whether `libsail` takes this on is for sail's tracker.

## The serial fixes do not wait on this

nail-fc2ac4 and nail-65ce8f add parallelism around the existing parsers and change no parsing code. `write_mmseqs_sequence_database` iterates with the serial `Database::iter`. `build_pipeline` calls `p7hmm.iter()` with the `par_iter()` line commented out beside it. A later move to `Framed` keeps the same rayon loop.
